    Volumes 0, I, II and III are closed: forty chapters, from a single bit to a program that survives contact with files, processes, networks and power cuts. Volume IV — the interpreter laid open — is under way: chapters 1–6 built — the reader now has a working tokenizer, parser, compiler and a virtual machine with frames and recursion — and by its end the reader has a working interpreter for a small language of their own.

    The order of Volume III

    Volume 0 already taught processes, the kernel boundary, scheduling and virtual memory, because Python could not be explained honestly without them. Volume III therefore deepens those subjects rather than introducing them, and is ordered so that the cost model comes before the concurrency that depends on it:

    III.1 ✓
    Opening the world — files, with, and where text becomes bytes
    III.2 ✓
    The cost of speaking — buffering, file descriptors, and counting system calls
    III.3 ✓
    Where things live — paths, directories, and the differences between operating systems
    III.4 ✓
    Memory that isn’t there — pages, page faults, memory mapping. Deepens Chapter 0.4
    III.5 ✓
    Programs starting programs — spawning processes, exit codes, pipes
    III.6 ✓
    Two things at once — threads, the global interpreter lock, and what parallel really means
    III.7 ✓
    Waiting without stopping — cooperative concurrency, built on the suspended frames of Chapter II.5
    III.8 ✓
    Talking to strangers — networks and sockets: bytes, latency and failure
    III.9 ✓
    Making it last — persistence, durability, atomic writes, databases and transactions
    III.10 ✓
    Who is allowed — permissions, trust boundaries and the security of an open door

    Why Volume II was reordered, not retrofitted

    The original manuscript taught cache lines before registers, branch prediction before the program counter, and profiling before processes and scheduling existed. It also postponed testing and debugging until after extensive micro-optimisation — which teaches a learner to measure the speed of a program nobody has proved correct.

    Patching chapters in that order cannot fix it, because the fault is the order. Volume II was therefore built to this sequence — testing second, cache locality and profiling last:

    II.1 ✓
    Membership and making — sets as hash tables without values; comprehensions. First honest look at how work grows
    II.2 ✓
    Proving it works — assertions and tests. Early, deliberately: measuring an unproven program measures the speed of a wrong answer
    II.3 ✓
    Finding the fault — debugging as a discipline: reading the traceback, bisecting, inspecting state
    II.4 ✓
    Rooms in the house — modules and packages; what import actually does
    II.5 ✓
    One at a time — iterators and generators; cashes the FOR_ITER promise from I.5
    II.6 ✓
    Functions that call themselves — recursion, built on I.8's frames; where the stack region ends
    II.7 ✓
    Types of your own — classes and protocols; why + behaved differently in I.2
    II.8 ✓
    Counting the cost — algorithmic complexity, made precise. Only now, with correct programs to compare
    II.9 ✓
    Under the list and the dict — dynamic arrays and hash tables in full; discharges I.6 and I.10's Level 3
    II.10 ✓
    Putting things in order — sorting, and why a key function was enough
    II.11 ✓
    Who cleans up — memory management, reference counting, garbage collection
    II.12 ✓
    Distance costs time — cache locality. Last but one, deliberately: needs Volume 0's RAM and II.11's layout to mean anything
    II.13 ✓
    Measure, then change — profiling and optimisation. Last, deliberately: needs processes, scheduling, complexity and tests to be honest

    Volume III, and why it deepens rather than repeats

    Processes, scheduling, context switching and virtual memory were all taught in Volume 0, because Python cannot be explained honestly without them. Volume III does not teach them again — it opens them up, now that there is a program with real work to do at the boundary. Everything here lights floor 12.

    III.1 ✓

    III.2 ✓
